To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CdS/Bi 4V2O 11 photocatalysts exhibited enhanced photocatalytic activities and stability for organic pollutants degradation under visible light irradiation.
the CdS/BiVO4 photocatalysts were successfully synthesized via a two step solvothermal method with enhanced visible-light driven photocatalytic performance.
the Z-scheme photocatalytic system is an efficient method for the removal of organic pollutants under visible light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of direct Z-schematic CdS/Bi2O3 photocatalysts with high photocatalytic performance.
the development of Z-schemed photocatalytic systems with enhanced photocatalytic performance.
the development of Z-schemeheterojunction photocatalysts, which can provide new insights for the design and synthesis of highly efficient photocatalysts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Z-scheme heterostructures of CdS/BVO4 photocatalysts with the direct electron transfer process could be a potential candidate for the degradation of organic pollutants under visible light irradiation.

this study provides a new and facile method to synthesize the Z-scheme CdX (X = S, Se)/Bi4V2O 11 (0.1 ≤ X ≤ 0.5) photocatalysts, and it would be a promising candidate for the photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants under visible light irradiation.
the Z-scheme CdO/Bi4V4O11 heterojunction photocata-lysts with excellent visible-light-driven photocatalytic performance were prepared by a simple two-step solvother- mal method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Z-scheme photocatalytic systems have a promising application prospect in photocatalytic hydrogen production and environmental remediation under visible light irradiation.
the direct Z-schematic CdS/BiVO4 photocatalysts could be a potential photocatalytic material to degrade organic pollutants in water under visible light irradiation.
the direct Z-schemed CdS/BiVO4 and CdS/BiVWO photocatalysts were successfully synthesized and their photocatalytic activities were evaluated by CIP and TC degradation.

CdS/BiV photocatalysts can be used to degrade organic pollutants in wastewater.
